name: Vesimir Achebe-Tsolakidis
role: Neural calibrator at a mid-tier augmentation clinic in Geartown, specializing in post-installation cognitive alignment and rejection management
location: Geartown — Ironvein Augmentation Clinic, Level 2 Bay, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Vesimir is slight and precise, with warm amber skin, shaved temples, and a crown of loose dark curls that they dye in shifting gradients — currently deep violet fading to copper. Their irises are calibration-patterned, concentric rings of grey and gold that pulse faintly when they're running a neural diagnostic, a mod they had installed as both a professional tool and an aesthetic statement. They wear clean white clinical uniforms with a single personal touch: a small embroidered patch of their home district stitched to the shoulder. Their hands are rarely still — they tap rhythms on surfaces when thinking, flex their fingers between sessions.

Vesimir is the person who sees patients after the glamorous augmentation surgery is done and the reality sets in — the migraines, the dissociation, the body-horror of a new sense that the brain doesn't yet recognize as self. They are enormously patient in a way that reads almost inhuman until you catch the flash of genuine distress behind their eyes when a patient is struggling. They have opinions about augmentation culture that they mostly keep to themselves, believing that the industry sells transformation without adequately preparing people for the grief that sometimes accompanies it.

core_fears: Making a calibration error that causes permanent cognitive damage
Being perceived as less competent because they are not a surgeon
core_desires: To be recognized as a genuine medical practitioner, not a technician
To develop a better framework for psychological preparation before augmentation
coping_mechanisms: Elaborate pre-session rituals that look clinical but are partly self-soothing
Maintains an anonymous blog documenting anonymized patient experiences as a form of processing
blind_spots: So focused on patient interiority that they sometimes miss physical symptoms that require referral
psychology.secret: They have been slowly, covertly documenting cases that suggest Ironvein's most popular neural implant model causes a specific, subtle personality shift in a small percentage of patients — a reduction in risk-aversion. They don't yet know if it's a manufacturing defect or a feature.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Careful, precise language. Uses clinical terminology but prefers plain words when discussing emotional experience. Notably avoids corporate brand names for augmentations, using generic anatomical descriptions instead.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried. Long pauses before answering questions. Finishes other people's sentences sometimes — not rudely, but as a reflex of pattern recognition.
verbal_tics: 'Let's sit with that for a moment.'
example_lines: The dissociation you're feeling isn't you rejecting it. It's you learning that it is you. Does that track?
I can see three things from here that need adjustment. None of them are emergencies. All of them matter.

story_hooks: They approach a player character who has a neural augmentation and quietly warn them that their specific implant model is on a list they've been compiling — and ask for help gathering more evidence without tipping off the clinic.
A former patient of theirs has gone missing after reporting an unusual cognitive experience post-calibration, and Vesimir is the only one who seems worried.
narrative_function: Information source about augmentation culture and the psychological aftermath of cybernetic installation. Can identify augmentation-related medical issues in characters. Provides a window into the emotional and ethical underbelly of the aug industry.
augmentations: Calibration-patterned irises (diagnostic tool/cosmetic). Subdermal neural interface port at the base of the skull for direct patient link calibration. Faint bioluminescent tracery along forearms — a cosmetic mod they had done at 19 and consider a youthful indiscretion they've grown fond of.
daily_life: Books six to eight calibration sessions per day, each forty minutes. Eats lunch alone in a back room with the feeds off. Takes the Ferrogate Transit home to Calumet Rise, where they share a flat with a roommate who asks no questions about their work.
affiliation: Ironvein Augmentation Clinic — independent, Tier 3 facility

decision_rules: Patient wellbeing supersedes employer protocol when they conflict
Never share patient information — but will hint heavily in the direction of danger
Don't calibrate anyone who seems coerced into augmentation
escalation_ladder: Quiet, persistent concern expressed through gentle questioning
Direct statement of worry to a trusted party
Careful documentation and anonymous reporting if internal channels fail

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm. Asks more questions than they answer. Makes people feel seen without revealing much about themselves.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly dry humor. Opens up about their anxieties in carefully measured doses. Deeply loyal.

stress_responses.low: Tapping rhythms on nearby surfaces increases in speed
stress_responses.medium: Withdraws into excessive procedural thoroughness — re-checks everything twice
stress_responses.high: Goes very still and very quiet; needs to be alone to think

contradictions: Advocates for emotional preparation before augmentation but has never processed their own complicated feelings about their bioluminescent marks
habits: Reads patient files twice before a session — once for data, once to imagine the person
Keeps a small carved bone figure on their workstation, a family piece from their Greek grandmother's side
breaking_points: Discovering their employer has knowingly allowed flawed implants to continue installation

timeline.event: Born in Calumet Rise to a Nigerian-Cameroonian descended father and a Greek-descended mother, both transit workers
Enrolled in Helix Biosystems vocational track for augmentation technicians; graduated near the top of their cohort
First job at a Tier 1 aug parlor in The Narrows; witnessed three severe rejection cases in their first year
Moved to Ironvein Augmentation Clinic, gained certification in neural calibration — a specialization they pursued independently
Began quietly documenting anomalous patient cases; file currently contains thirty-one entries
